subject: Performance SLO discovery + suggested cost/perf playbook
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Ortiz <janelle.ortiz@acme-retail.com>, Marco Silva <marco.silva@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30 09:12 PDT
Subject: Post-call recap — perf targets and next steps

Hi Janelle / Marco — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap so we have a clear set of inputs to run a qualification pass and propose an ops plan. I captured notes while they were fresh; please flag anything I've missed.

High-level asks from Acme (as discussed):
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end generation <= 300 ms for synchronous requests (short form responses, ~50-150 tokens).
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for conversational product — client expects first token within 120-150 ms, and subsequent tokens every ~120-200 ms.
- Throughput: sustained 800 QPS for peak storefront events, with occasional bursts to 2k QPS.
- Concurrency: target concurrency of ~160 simultaneous sessions during peak.
- Cost objective: keep incremental inference cost within the economics we discussed (we'll use the prompt size and token projections you provided).

Immediate deliverables we (Redwood) will provide:
1) SLO matrix + perf run plan (attached SLO-matrix-Acme.xlsx, perf-run-plan.pdf).
2) Recommended cost/perf levers tailored to the workload (continuous batching settings, cache strategy, quantization profiles, model variants).
3) A small benchmark run using your representative prompt set (please confirm sample-payloads.json attached is representative).

High-level options we discussed (short rationale):
- Continuous batching: improves GPU utilization and lowers token cost at the expense of small added latency; we will tune max batch delay windows to keep p95 under 300 ms.
- Prefix / KV cache reuse: effective when prompts reuse context (e.g., multi-turn sessions); can reduce repeated compute for long histories.
- Quantization profiles: int8 and 4-bit options provide substantial cost wins; int8 is lowest risk for latency stability, 4-bit (q4) can reduce cost further but needs validation for quality.
- Model variants: a smaller, optimized variant for high-throughput non-chat traffic, larger variant for high-quality conversational flows; routing policy can keep tail latency tight while minimizing cost.

Request from Acme: please share a 24–48 hour sample of real-ish traffic (anonymized) or confirm the two sample payloads attached are representative. Also confirm which of the two routes will be primary (product A: realtime chat; product B: batch recommendations).

Next meeting: propose 1-week cadence for the qualification sprint — start perf runs Wed 6/2, internal sync on 6/4, demo of initial numbers 6/9. Happy to move dates if that doesn't work.

Thanks — r

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

Date: 2027-05-30 10:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — perf targets and next steps

Thanks Rishi — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 800 QPS sustained is for our US storefront region only; EU will be lower initially (~120 QPS).
- Payload sizes: median prompt ~90 tokens, 95th ~320 tokens; responses average ~60 tokens. I've attached two anonymized example payloads (included in sample-payloads.json) — they are representative.
- For streaming, first token latency is critical for perceived responsiveness; <150 ms is ideal but we can accept up to 200 ms if overall throughput is maintained.

We can provide a 48-hour slice of anonymized traffic by end of day Tuesday (6/1). 6/2 start for perf runs works for us; please include an ETA for the initial benchmark results.

Also, procurement asked for a rough cost delta between: 1) int8 quant + batching vs 2) q4_0 + aggressive batching + prefix caching. A ballpark % impact would help with internal budgeting.

— Janelle
Director, Product — Acme Retail
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Janelle Ortiz <janelle.ortiz@acme-retail.com>, Marco Silva <marco.silva@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-05-30 13:20 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — perf targets and next steps

Adding the technical plan and an initial estimate. I'll own the perf run and provide numbers for the two quantization cases Janelle requested.

Planned qualification sprint (summary):
- Day 1 (6/2): baseline runs on the full model (fp16) with conservative batching disabled to capture raw single-request latency distribution. Collect p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.
- Day 2 (6/3): enable continuous batching with incremental max_delay_ms = [10, 25, 50] and measure p95 vs throughput tradeoff. Also run with prefix cache enabled for multi-turn flows.
- Day 3 (6/4): run quantized profiles: int8 (stable), q4_0 (aggressive) — measure quality regression against a small eval set + latency.
- Day 4 (6/5): run routing scenarios mixing model variants: small-gen for high-throughput recommendation calls, large-gen for primary chat flows; measure tail latency and unit cost.

Preliminary ballpark cost deltas (very approximate; we will produce measured numbers):
- int8 + moderate batching: ~25–35% cost reduction vs fp16 baseline, with minimal p95 impact in most cases.
- q4_0 + aggressive batching + prefix cache: ~45–60% cost reduction vs fp16 baseline, but expect quality and occasional increased variance in tail latency — requires evaluation against your key prompts.

Initial latency guidance: with continuous batching tuned (max_delay_ms <= 25) and int8 quant, we expect to meet p95 <= 300 ms for median prompt sizes (~90 tokens) at ~800 QPS in a dedicated pool with conservative autoscaling buffers. Streaming first-token latency is most sensitive to batching delay — we'll configure a 'streaming fast-path' with small batch window (<= 10 ms) for those routes.

Action items for Acme:
- Confirm sample payloads + provide 48-hour anonymized slice (Janelle).
- Identify the canonical prompt set for quality eval (5–10 prompts).

Our deliverables by 6/9 demo: measured p95/p99, throughput curves, cost-per-1k-token estimates for fp16/int8/q4_0, and suggested routing + autoscale policy.

Ben

Great — thanks everyone for the rapid responses. Confirming the plan:
- Acme provides 48h anonymized traffic + canonical prompt set by 6/1 EOD.
- Redwood starts baseline perf runs 6/2.
- Internal sync (Redwood <> Acme) 6/4 to review mid-run observations; 30m slot (I sent a calendar invite).
- Demo of initial measured numbers and recommended playbook 6/9.

Ben will own the perf runs and will post raw run artifacts to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cPerfPlan). Priya will draft a scoped proposal for a Dedicated pool config (capacity, autoscale policy, and fallback routing). Karthik will prepare suggested A/B routing configs that minimize tail latency while capturing cost savings.

If procurement needs a formal statement of work or rough pricing tiers early, Priya can draft a short 1‑pager prior to 6/9.

Thanks — looking forward to the runs.
